# governance-factory — the tool reference (v6)

> One page that describes the tool as it is — for whoever continues it from a
> separate conversation and hands prompts down to this repo. Every table below
> is rendered from `factory.yaml` by `gov.py render`, so this file cannot say
> something the tool does not do; `gov.py lint` refuses a stale copy. What is
> project-variable is deliberately absent: it lives in the project repo.

## 1. What it is

A **pure, project-agnostic analysis factory**: this checkout is a stateless tool. It reads
one **project repo** — named by `$GOV_PROJECT_CHECKOUT` (default
`../governance-shared`) — and writes only there: the project's `project.yaml`
names the active domain profile; the profile is data (`profiles/<id>.yaml`, validated
against this tool's `profiles/_schema.yaml`); the analysis, the decisions, the split packages and the
tracks' own partitions are all in that repo, one writer per path. Switching projects is pointing the
variable at another checkout. Boundary: **analysis-only** — it never implements, never
audits an implementation, never runs tests inside the line.

The binding rules are `shared/CONSTITUTION.md` (C1–C6). The single source of every stage, pass,
gate, lane, naming, id-grammar and marker fact is `factory.yaml`; every generated file
(`SKILL.md`, `.claude/commands/`, `README.md`, `shared/START-HERE.md`, this page, the project's
`analysis/platform/PROJECT-OVERVIEW.md`) is produced by `gov.py render` and kept fresh by `gov.py lint`.

## 2. The project repo

<!-- RENDER:project-layout -->
| Path | What lives there |
|---|---|
| `project.yaml` | the project's facts: profile id, consumer repos (user-edited) |
| `profiles` | the domain profile(s): `<id>.yaml` + `<id>/knowledge/` |
| `analysis/domain` | `domain-profile.md` — the entry gate |
| `analysis/platform` | `project-registry.md`, system tests, the rendered overview |
| `analysis/modules` | `{MOD}/[vN/]` — every stage artifact, `_state/`, `_inputs/`, `manifest.json` |
| `analysis/decisions` | `{MOD}/` — the ADR stream, dialogue decisions included |
| `analysis/platform/PROJECT-OVERVIEW.md` | the rendered profile summary + phase tables |
<!-- /RENDER:project-layout -->

Ownership is enforced, not conventional: the project's `CODEOWNERS` is derived from this table,
most specific wins, and a factory regeneration may delete only what the deepest matching partition
says is the factory's (`gov.py run-pass --regenerate`).

<!-- RENDER:partitions -->
| Partition | Path in the project repo | Writer | Readers |
|---|---|---|---|
| `platform` | `platform` | `factory` | all |
| `analysis` | `analysis/modules/{MOD}` | `factory` | `factory` |
| `api-docs` | `backend/modules/{MOD}/api-docs` | `backend` | all |
| `backend-packages` | `backend/modules/{MOD}/packages` | `factory` | `backend` |
| `frontend-packages` | `frontend/modules/{MOD}/packages` | `factory` | `frontend` |
| `backend` | `backend/modules/{MOD}` | `backend` | `backend` |
| `frontend` | `frontend/modules/{MOD}` | `frontend` | `frontend` |
<!-- /RENDER:partitions -->

Every consumer mounts the project repo as a submodule and **pins a commit**: a delivered version
does not move under a consumer, an upgrade is a reviewed pointer bump, and `gov.py fetch-inputs`
records the project commit it read a track's publication at (`{file}.meta.json`,
`manifest.json → status.inputs`). `gov.py sparse --track <t>` narrows what a
consumer sees to what it may read; `gov.py sync` reports where the project repo stands and which
consumer is behind it.

<!-- /RENDER:stages -->

Passes: **pass 1** = P0 → P0.5 → P1 → P2 → P3.1 → gate:pass-1 → split (track `backend`); **pass 2** = P3.2 → gate:pass-2 → split → tag (track `frontend`, requires api-docs fetched back).
A stage runs one protocol — state → brief → dispatch → write → analyze → commit — owned by `gov.py`
(`shared/GOVERNANCE-CORE.md` §6). Questions are allowed only where `stages[*].questions` says so and
are closed inside the lane's dialogue; after that, ambiguity is an ADR (`factory.ambiguity`), and
every decision a dialogue settles is persisted as an ADR too (`factory.dialogue`, status
`RESOLVED-IN-DIALOGUE`).

Standalone, outside the line, never a gate:

| Stage | Title | Pass | Questions | Lane | Inputs | Produces | Owns IDs |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `test-gen` | Test Generation | standalone | forbidden | `test-gen` | `srs`, `backend-execution-plan?`, `frontend-execution-plan?`, `registry-srs`, `registry-db?`, `registry-exec-fe?` | `backend-test-plan-{mod}.md`, `frontend-test-plan-{mod}.md`, `test-execution-manifest-{mod}.md`, `system-test-index-{profile}.md` | `TC` |
| `api-verify` | API Verification (post-implementation) | standalone | forbidden | `analysis` | `api-docs`, `test-execution-manifest?` | `api-verify-{mod}.py`, `api-verify-report-{mod}.md` | — |

## 4. Gates and the analyze policy

<!-- RENDER:gates -->
| Gate | When | Type | Lanes | Requires analyze | On REVISE |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `prd-approval` | after `P0.5` | human-approval | — | — | `—` |
| `pass-1` | after `P3.1` | review | `review-pass` | clean | `merge-review-notes` |
| `pass-2` | after `P3.2` | review | `review-pass` | clean | `merge-review-notes` |
<!-- /RENDER:gates -->

`gov.py analyze` implements every clause of `shared/ARTIFACT-CONTRACTS.md` against the module's
generated current state; a gate opens only with no finding at CRITICAL/MAJOR
(`analyze.blocking`). The **maturity** clauses (ambiguity, measurable criteria, lifecycle coverage,
unwanted paths, screen states, glossary) fire at `analyze.maturity_severity` = `MINOR`
— recorded for the reviewer, never closing a gate on their own. Every report, gate record and the
module's execution state carry the coverage ratios of `analyze.coverage`
(`us-req`, `req-ac`, `req-api`, `req-ux`).

The review is one brief (`reviewers/pass-review.md`) — the analyze report, an adversarial reading
(§3.5), a scorecard on unambiguous, verifiable, complete, consistent, singular, feasible, traceable (0–3,
threshold 2) and one JSON verdict in APPROVE / REVISE / ESCALATE.
A REVISE is applied by the gate's `on_revise` lane, re-analyzed and re-gated at most
1 time(s), then ESCALATES to a human.

<!-- RENDER:review-rubric -->
Scale 0–3; every attribute must score ≥ 2 to APPROVE; verdicts `APPROVE`, `REVISE`, `ESCALATE`; at most 1 REVISE per finding before ESCALATE.

- `unambiguous`
- `verifiable`
- `complete`
- `consistent`
- `singular`
- `feasible`
- `traceable`
<!-- /RENDER:review-rubric -->

## 5. Lanes and the runner

<!-- RENDER:lanes -->
| Lane | Implementers | Effort | Mode | Dialogue |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `analysis` | `claude:opus` | high | — | — |
| `analysis-dialogue` | `claude:opus`, `claude:sonnet` | high | — | max 4 rounds, converge on *mutually-acceptable* |
| `review-pass` | `claude:sonnet`, `claude:opus` | medium | read-only | max 2 rounds, converge on *merged-scorecard* |
| `merge-review-notes` | `claude:sonnet` | low | — | — |
| `test-gen` | `claude:opus` | high | — | — |
<!-- /RENDER:lanes -->

Every reasoning step is a brief on a lane; every mechanical step (state, analyze, split, tag,
publish, sync) is a direct `gov.py` operation. `$GOV_RUNNER` chooses the runner: `cmd`
runs `$GOV_RUNNER_CMD` once per round — the shipped template is
`governance-tools/runner/claude_delegate.sh {brief} {lane} {model} {read_only_flag} {out}`, which drives the claude-delegate
relay and hands the final response back; `{model}` is
mandatory because a dialogue lane alternates implementers. `manual` writes the brief and waits for the
operator (exit 2); `fake` is the test hook. In `cmd` mode nothing waits: `gov.py next -m MOD --run`
executes the single next protocol step until the version is complete, stopping only at the human
decision points, a `[QUESTION]` in a questions-forbidden stage, a BLOCKED ADR, a blocking finding or
an ESCALATE.

## 6. Identity, markers, versions

<!-- RENDER:ids -->
Pattern `{prefix}-{MOD}-{seq}`, sequence width 3.

| Atom | Meaning | Owner | Traces to | Requires |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `POL` | business policy | `P0` | — | — |
| `US` | user story | `P0.5` | `POL` | — |
| `REQ` | requirement (EARS) | `P1` | `US` | `AC` |
| `AC` | acceptance criterion (Given/When/Then) | `P1` | `REQ` | — |
| `ENT` | entity | `P1` | — | — |
| `RULE` | business rule | `P1` | `REQ` | — |
| `DBF` | db field | `P2` | `REQ`, `ENT` | — |
| `XM` | cross-module dependency | `P2` | `REQ` | — |
| `API` | api endpoint | `P3.1` | `REQ`, `DBF` | — |
| `QR` | query reference | `P3.1` | — | — |
| `UXD` | ux decision | `P3.2` | `REQ`, `AC` | — |
| `SCR` | screen | `P3.2` | `REQ`, `UXD` | — |
| `SCR-REQ` | screen requirement | `P1` | `REQ` | — |
| `TC` | test case | `test-gen` | `AC`, `XM`, `UXD` | — |
| `ADR` | analysis decision record | `any` | — | — |
| `CS` | change set | `versioning` | — | — |
<!-- /RENDER:ids -->

Requirements follow EARS (`factory.ids.ears`):
<!-- RENDER:ears -->
| Pattern | Statement regex |
|---|---|
| ubiquitous | `^The system shall ` |
| state | `^While .+, the system shall ` |
| event | `^When .+, the system shall ` |
| optional | `^Where .+, the system shall ` |
| unwanted | `^If .+, then the system shall ` |
<!-- /RENDER:ears -->

Execution plans carry the marker grammar the split reads (`shared/MARKER-PROTOCOL.md`); the phase
keys are the project profile's and appear in its `analysis/platform/PROJECT-OVERVIEW.md`:
<!-- RENDER:markers -->
Schema version **2**, syntax `html-comment`, attributes `traces`.

| Kind | Level | Allowed parents | Identity | Scope |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `PHASE` | 1 | top level | keys from profile | all |
| `SUB` | 2 | `PHASE` | phase-qualified label | all |
| `API` | 3 | `PHASE`, `SUB` | atom `API` | tracks: backend |
| `XM` | 3 | `PHASE`, `SUB` | atom `XM` | tracks: backend |
| `TC` | 3 | `PHASE`, `SUB` | atom `TC` | plans: test |
<!-- /RENDER:markers -->

Versions: `v{version}` folders in the project repo are the authority
(`versioning.authority`); v1 is the module's base folder, vN holds only what changed plus a change
manifest, and `gov.py state` folds them into `_state/` — the only thing
an engine reads. A frozen version is tagged `{mod}-v{version}` **in the project repo**.

## 9. Constitution enforcement

`gov.py lint` refuses: a profile that does not validate against the schema (C5); a removed concept
or a profile's own vocabulary typed into the tool (C2); a stage id, phase key or id prefix as a
Python literal (C2); a generated file that differs from a fresh render (C1); a command file the
tool did not generate; and — because the tool is project-neutral — the active project's identity
anywhere in the tool's docs. Tests build a temporary project repo of their own (`governance-tools/tests`);
none depends on a committed project.
